text: 阿片战争是19世纪中叶大清帝国与西方列强之间发生的两场冲突。
en: The Opium War(s) are two conflicts that occurred in the mid-19th century between the Great Qing Empire and the Western powers.

text: 因第一场冲突由鸦片禁令而引发，而第二场冲突被认为是第一场冲突的延续，故被统称为鸦片战争。
en: Because the first conflict was triggered by an opium ban, and the second conflict is considered a continuation of the first conflict, therefore [they] are collectively called the Opium War.

text: 第一次鸦片战争于1840年英国对中国发动的一场非正义的战争，结束于1842年两国政府签订《南京条约》。
en: The First Opium War [was] an unjust war launched by Britain against China in 1840, ending in 1842 with the two countries' governments signing the Treaty of Nanking.

text: 这次事件是由清政府强制执行鸦片禁令而引发的，其中包括销毁英国商人和英国东印度公司拥有的鸦片库存。
en: This event was triggered by the Qing government's forcible enforcement of the opium ban, which included destroying the opium stocks owned by British merchants and the British East India Company.

text: 英国政府的回应是派出海军远征队，迫使清朝政府支付赔款并允许鸦片贸易。
en: The British government's response was to send a naval expeditionary force, forcing the Qing government to pay indemnities and allow the opium trade.

text: 1856年至1860年，英国和法国对华发动第二次鸦片战争，迫使中国鸦片合法化。
en: From 1856 to 1860, Britain and France launched the Second Opium War against China, forcing China [to] legalize opium.

text: 在两次战争中，欧洲军队凭借军事优势多次比较轻松地战胜清军，结果清政府被迫签署不平等条约，迫使中国向西方商人开放特定的通商口岸（包括上海），给予西方列强优惠的关税、贸易优惠、赔款和领土割让。
en: In the two wars, European armies, relying on military superiority, repeatedly defeated the Qing army fairly easily; as a result the Qing government was forced to sign unequal treaties, forcing China to open specific trading ports (including Shanghai) to Western merchants, and grant the Western powers preferential tariffs, trade preferences, indemnities and territorial cession.

text: 两次冲突，加上所谓“百年国耻”期间强加的各种条约，削弱了清朝政府的权威。
en: The two conflicts, plus the various treaties imposed during the so-called 'Century of Humiliation', weakened the authority of the Qing government.

text: 此外，中国将香港主权割让给大英帝国，大英帝国对该地区的控制一直持续到1997年。
en: In addition, China ceded sovereignty of Hong Kong to the British Empire; the British Empire's control over the area lasted until 1997.

text: 在此期间，中国经济也因战争而略有收缩，但太平天国之乱和同治陕甘回乱对经济的影响要大得多。
en: During this period, China's economy also shrank slightly because of the wars, but the Taiping Rebellion's and the Tongzhi Shaanxi-Gansu Hui revolt's effect on the economy was much greater.

text: 1840年，中国与英国爆发第一次鸦片战争，双方因为鸦片贸易问题爆发了战争。
en: In 1840, China and Britain broke out [into] the First Opium War; the two sides broke out into war because of the opium trade issue.

text: 18世纪，中国对欧洲享有贸易顺差，通过瓷器、丝绸和茶叶换取白银。
en: In the 18th century, China enjoyed a trade surplus with Europe, exchanging porcelain, silk and tea for silver.

text: 光合作用也称光能合成（英语：photosynthesis），是食物网基层的一些细胞生物利用感光色素吸收环境光（如日光）获取光能将二氧化碳、水或硫化氢等无机物转变成可以储存化学能的有机物（如碳水化合物）的生物过程，根据化学反应所产生的副产品可分为产氧光合作用和不产氧光合作用两类，分别使用不同的感光色素，而且会因为不同环境改变反应速率。
en: Photosynthesis, also called light-energy synthesis (English: photosynthesis), is the biological process by which some cellular organisms at the base of the food web use photosensitive pigments to absorb ambient light (such as sunlight) to obtain light energy to convert inorganic substances such as carbon dioxide, water or hydrogen sulfide into organic substances (such as carbohydrates) that can store chemical energy; according to the by-products produced by the chemical reaction it can be divided into oxygenic and anoxygenic photosynthesis, which respectively use different photosensitive pigments, and it will change its reaction rate because of different environments.

text: 通俗意义上的“光合作用”主要指自元古宙后期至今一直占据地球生物圈主流地位的产氧光合作用。
en: 'Photosynthesis' in the popular sense mainly refers to oxygenic photosynthesis, which from the late Proterozoic until now has continuously occupied the dominant position of Earth's biosphere.

text: 地球上的光合作用始于太古宙中期的原始微生物菌落中，使得自养生物不再依赖海底热泉提供化合作用所需的热能、无机物和酸碱度，生物圈得以脱离深海向浅海和潮间带扩展。
en: Photosynthesis on Earth began in primitive microbial colonies of the mid-Archean, making autotrophs no longer depend on seafloor hydrothermal vents to provide the heat, inorganic matter and pH needed for chemosynthesis, [and] the biosphere was able to leave the deep sea and expand toward shallow seas and the intertidal zone.

text: 光合作用也因此彻底取代化合作用成为主流初级生产模式。
en: Photosynthesis therefore also completely replaced chemosynthesis to become the mainstream primary production mode.

text: 初期的光合作用主要是不产氧的，形式包括直接吸收日光驱动跨膜蛋白生产三磷酸腺苷和通过分解硫化物（如硫化氢）生产碳水化合物；但随着蓝绿菌和其后来与真核细胞发生内共生后演化出的原始质体生物（藻类和植物）的出现和演化辐射，通过分解水来进行固碳的产氧光合作用在元古宙成为主流。
en: Early photosynthesis was mainly anoxygenic, its forms including directly absorbing sunlight to drive transmembrane proteins to produce ATP and producing carbohydrates by decomposing sulfides (such as hydrogen sulfide); but with the appearance and evolutionary radiation of cyanobacteria and of the primitive plastid organisms (algae and plants) that evolved after cyanobacteria later entered endosymbiosis with eukaryotic cells, oxygenic photosynthesis, which fixes carbon by splitting water, became mainstream in the Proterozoic.

text: 此类光合自养者使用卟啉衍生物——叶绿素作为反应中心的感光色素，主要吸收可见光谱中的红蓝色波段（不吸收绿光，因此呈现绿色），并以此光分解水分子获取氢正离子将二氧化碳聚合成碳水化合物，其过程中会释放游离态的单质氧气作为副产物，其理论最高能量转换效率约为4.6～6％，实际效率仅有1.9～2.5％。
en: Such photoautotrophs use a porphyrin derivative, chlorophyll, as the photosensitive pigment of the reaction centre, mainly absorbing the red and blue bands of the visible spectrum (not absorbing green light, therefore appearing green), and with it photolyse water molecules to obtain hydrogen cations to polymerize carbon dioxide into carbohydrates; in the process free elemental oxygen is released as a by-product; its theoretical maximum energy conversion efficiency is about 4.6-6%, actual efficiency only 1.9-2.5%.

text: 光合自养者生产的有机物可以被不参与初级生产的异养生物（消费者和分解者）摄入并消化，然后通过食物链将生物能传递给其它营养级更高的生物供其生存和种群繁衍。
en: The organic matter produced by photoautotrophs can be ingested and digested by heterotrophs (consumers and decomposers) not taking part in primary production, and then via the food chain bio-energy is passed on to other organisms of higher trophic levels for their survival and population reproduction.

text: 光合作用因此是除深海以外绝大多数生态系统赖以维持的关键，也是地球碳循环和氧循环中最重要的一环。
en: Photosynthesis is therefore the key on which the vast majority of ecosystems apart from the deep sea rely for maintenance, and also the most important link in Earth's carbon cycle and oxygen cycle.

text: 许多现生的微生物仍保留了不产氧光合作用的初级生产方式。
en: Many extant microorganisms still retain the primary production mode of anoxygenic photosynthesis.

text: 一些厌氧菌（如绿硫细菌、紫细菌、酸杆菌和太阳杆菌）主要用菌绿素分解硫化氢获取氢离子和二氧化碳发生固碳反应并产生碳水化合物和硫，这种光合方式曾在硫化缺氧的元古宙中期十亿年期间占据生物圈主流；除此之外，一些古菌（如盐杆菌）可以用基于视黄醛的视紫质（菌紫质）来吸收绿光（因此呈现紫色）驱动离子泵直接生产三磷酸腺苷，这种更简单直接的光合作用很可能在古太古代就已经出现（参见紫色地球假说），是地球史上最早的一种利用光能生产有机物的生化现象，但在大氧化事件和休伦大冰期之后被彻底边缘化，现今这类古菌只能作为嗜极生物存在于其它生物都难以生存的火山硫磺温泉与缺氧的高盐湖泊和盐田中。
en: Some anaerobic bacteria (such as green sulfur bacteria, purple bacteria, acidobacteria and heliobacteria) mainly use bacteriochlorophyll to split hydrogen sulfide to obtain hydrogen ions and carry out carbon fixation with carbon dioxide, producing carbohydrates and sulfur; this mode of photosynthesis once dominated the biosphere for a billion years in the sulfidic, anoxic mid-Proterozoic; besides this, some archaea (such as Halobacterium) can use retinal-based rhodopsin (bacteriorhodopsin) to absorb green light (therefore appearing purple) to drive ion pumps that directly produce ATP; this simpler and more direct photosynthesis very probably already appeared in the Paleoarchean (see Purple Earth hypothesis), and is the earliest biochemical phenomenon in Earth's history that uses light energy to produce organic matter, but after the Great Oxidation Event and the Huronian glaciation it was completely marginalized; today such archaea can only exist as extremophiles in volcanic sulfur hot springs and anoxic hypersaline lakes and salt pans where other organisms can hardly survive.

text: 虽然一些在光合作用中的步骤仍不能被完全理解，但是整体的光合方程式自19世纪以来是已知的。
en: Although some steps in photosynthesis still cannot be fully understood, the overall photosynthesis equation has been known since the 19th century.

text: 古希腊哲学家亚里士多德认为，植物生长所需的营养全来自土中。
en: The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle believed that the nutrients needed for plant growth all came from the soil.

text: 通货膨胀（英语：inflation），简称通胀（台湾简称为通膨），指整体价格或物价水平持续上涨的经济现象。
en: Inflation (English: inflation), abbreviated tongzhang (in Taiwan abbreviated tongpeng), refers to the economic phenomenon of the overall price or price level continuously rising.

text: 当整体物价水平上涨，人们的购买力就会减少。
en: When the overall price level rises, people's purchasing power will decrease.

text: 相反的经济现象是通货紧缩。
en: The opposite economic phenomenon is deflation.

text: 一般来说，通货膨胀发生的原因有商品供给不足（即商品短缺或生产率低下）、需求增加（即消费提升）、货币供给增加（即货币发行数量增加），只要其中的一种原因发生就有可能导致通胀，而通胀的幅度就看上述原因的增减程度而定。
en: Generally speaking, the causes of inflation are insufficient supply of goods (i.e. goods shortage or low productivity), increased demand (i.e. rising consumption), increased money supply (i.e. increased quantity of money issued); as long as one of these causes occurs it may lead to inflation, and the magnitude of inflation depends on the degree of increase or decrease of the above causes.

text: 通货膨胀与货币贬值不同，整体通货膨胀为特定经济体内之货币购买力的下降，而货币贬值为货币在不同经济体之间相对价值的降低。
en: Inflation differs from currency depreciation: overall inflation is the decline of a currency's purchasing power within a particular economy, while currency depreciation is the reduction of a currency's relative value between different economies.

text: 前者影响此货币在国内市场上的价值，而后者影响此货币在国际市场上的价值，两者之相关性为经济学上的争议之一。
en: The former affects this currency's value on the domestic market, while the latter affects this currency's value on the international market; the correlation of the two is one of the controversies in economics.

text: 因为不同物价影响不同人，通货膨胀有许多不同的衡量方式，最常见的两种衡量指数有衡量账面消费者物价的居民消费价格指数，以及衡量新出现的财货及服务的通货膨胀的GDP平减指数。
en: Because different prices affect different people, inflation has many different ways of measurement; the two most common measurement indices are the consumer price index, which measures book consumer prices, and the GDP deflator, which measures inflation of newly appearing goods and services.

text: 主流经济学家对于通货膨胀起因的看法可大略分为两派，“货币主义者”相信货币是通胀率数值最主要的影响，“凯恩斯主义者”相信货币、利率和产出间的相互作用才是最主要的影响，凯恩斯主义者也倾向除了一般标准消费性商品物价通胀外再另附上生产性商品（资本）通胀。
en: Mainstream economists' views on the causes of inflation can roughly be divided into two schools: 'monetarists' believe money is the most important influence on the inflation rate figure; 'Keynesians' believe the interaction among money, interest rates and output is the most important influence; Keynesians also tend to add productive-goods (capital) inflation besides general standard consumer-goods price inflation.

text: 其他理论，例如奥地利经济学派，相信通胀是中央银行增加货币供给导致。
en: Other theories, for example the Austrian School of economics, believe inflation is caused by central banks increasing the money supply.

text: 简单地说，当政府发行了过多货币时，货币便会贬值，而物价因而上升。
en: Simply put, when the government issues too much money, money will depreciate, and prices therefore rise.

text: 通货膨胀减缓（disinflation），意指通胀率的降低。
en: Inflation slowing (disinflation) means the reduction of the inflation rate.

text: 恶性通货膨胀，意指通胀失去控制，物价急遽增加。
en: Hyperinflation means inflation getting out of control [and] prices increasing sharply.

text: 周树人（1881年9月25日—1936年10月19日），原名周樟寿，字豫山、豫亭，后改字豫才，笔名鲁迅，浙江绍兴人，中国近代作家、设计师、新文化运动领袖之一。
en: Zhou Shuren (25 Sep 1881 - 19 Oct 1936), original name Zhou Zhangshou, courtesy name Yushan, Yuting, later changed courtesy name to Yucai, pen name Lu Xun, native of Shaoxing, Zhejiang, a modern Chinese writer, designer, and one of the leaders of the New Culture Movement.

text: 鲁迅生前创作了杂文、短中篇小说、文学、思想和社会评论、学术著作、自然科学著作、古代典籍校勘与研究、散文、现代散文诗、旧体诗、外国文学与学术翻译作品和木刻版画的研究，对于五四运动以后的中国社会与文化产生极大影响。
en: During his lifetime Lu Xun created essays, short and novella fiction, literary, intellectual and social criticism, scholarly works, natural-science works, collation and study of ancient classics, prose, modern prose poems, classical-style poems, translations of foreign literature and scholarship, and studies of woodcut prints, [and] exerted an enormous influence on Chinese society and culture after the May Fourth Movement.

text: 清光绪七年八月初三（1881年9月25日），鲁迅出生于浙江省绍兴府会稽县府城内东昌坊口（周家西门口西轴线上，今属绍兴市越城区鲁迅中路229号鲁迅故居西次间楼下，鲁迅纪念馆西侧）的书香门第，覆盆桥周氏家族，名为周樟寿。
en: On the 3rd day of the 8th month of Guangxu 7 (25 Sep 1881), Lu Xun was born into a scholarly family in Dongchangfangkou inside the prefectural city of Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang Province (on the west axis of the Zhou family's west gate, today part of Yuecheng District, Shaoxing City, No. 229 Lu Xun Middle Road, downstairs in the west side room of Lu Xun's Former Residence, west of the Lu Xun Memorial Hall), the Zhou clan of Fupenqiao, named Zhou Zhangshou.

text: 祖父周福清（1838—1904年），同治十年（1871年）进士，选翰林院庶吉士，江西金溪县知县，捐内阁中书。
en: [His] grandfather Zhou Fuqing (1838-1904), jinshi in the 10th year of Tongzhi (1871), selected as Hanlin Academy shujishi, magistrate of Jinxi County, Jiangxi, purchased [the rank of] Grand Secretariat secretary.

text: 父亲周伯宜（1861—1896），秀才出身。
en: [His] father Zhou Boyi (1861-1896), of xiucai background.

text: 鲁迅童年生活于百草园、咸亨酒店、外婆家一带的农村等地，成为后来鲁迅的两部小说集《呐喊》、《彷徨》和散文集《朝花夕拾》的重要素材来源。
en: In childhood Lu Xun lived in the Hundred-Grass Garden, Xianheng Tavern, the countryside around [his] maternal grandmother's home and other places, [which] became important source material for Lu Xun's later two story collections Nahan and Panghuang and the essay collection Zhaohua Xishi.

text: 鲁迅颇受进化论思想影响，爱读新思想的书，尤其是翻译的小说。
en: Lu Xun was considerably influenced by evolutionary-theory thought, loved reading books of new thought, especially translated fiction.

text: 鲁迅于10岁就读于家乡寿镜吾开设的私塾三味书屋。
en: At age 10 Lu Xun studied at the private school Sanwei Shuwu opened by Shou Jingwu in [his] hometown.

text: 1893年（光绪19年），周福清因为向浙江乡试主考官殷汝璋行贿，谋求其子周伯宜录取，被殷汝璋举报，而被革职下狱，鲁迅兄弟则被安插到离城有三十多里的皇甫庄大舅父的家中避难。
en: In 1893 (Guangxu 19), Zhou Fuqing, because [he] bribed the chief examiner of the Zhejiang provincial examination Yin Ruzhang, seeking admission for his son Zhou Boyi, was reported by Yin Ruzhang, and was dismissed and imprisoned; Lu Xun and his brothers were placed in the home of [their] eldest maternal uncle in Huangfuzhuang, more than thirty li from the city, to take refuge.

text: 周福清科举舞弊案判处了“斩监候”，周家为了使周福清得以活命，每年花费大笔资金疏通官府，直到八国联军事件之后，周福清才被赦免。
en: The Zhou Fuqing imperial-examination fraud case was sentenced to 'beheading after the autumn assizes'; the Zhou family, in order to keep Zhou Fuqing alive, spent large sums every year to bribe the officials, until after the Eight-Nation Alliance incident Zhou Fuqing was finally pardoned.

text: 但这八年的支出，周家家道衰落，同时期父亲周伯宜也重病在床，1896年病故。
en: But [through] these eight years' expenditure, the Zhou family's fortunes declined; in the same period [his] father Zhou Boyi was also seriously ill in bed, [and] died of illness in 1896.

text: 家庭的变故对鲁迅产生了深刻的影响。
en: The family's misfortunes had a profound influence on Lu Xun.

text: 春节，又称农历新年、中国新年、华人新年，是中国传统历法（农历）中的岁首，也是华人及全球汉字文化圈一年中最重要的传统节日。
en: The Spring Festival, also called the Lunar New Year, Chinese New Year, Huaren New Year, is the start of the year in China's traditional calendar (the lunar calendar), and also the most important traditional festival of the year for ethnic Chinese and the global Sinosphere.

text: 当代春节通常从农历腊月廿三持续庆祝至正月十五（元宵节），其中以除夕及正月初一最为隆重。
en: The contemporary Spring Festival is usually celebrated continuously from the 23rd of the twelfth lunar month to the 15th of the first month (Lantern Festival), among which New Year's Eve and the first day of the first month are the grandest.

text: 春节是以农历计算的中国传统新年，是汉族四大传统节日之一。
en: The Spring Festival is the traditional Chinese New Year calculated by the lunar calendar, [and] is one of the four great traditional festivals of the Han ethnic group.

text: 从明代开始，华夏新年节庆一般要到正月十五日元宵节之后才正式结束活动，有些地方的新年庆祝活动甚至到整个正月完结为止，其庆祝活动俗称过年、度岁等。
en: From the Ming dynasty on, the Huaxia New Year festivities generally only formally end their activities after the Lantern Festival on the 15th of the first month; in some places the New Year celebrations even [last] until the whole first month is over; its celebration activities are popularly called guonian, dusui, etc.

text: 辛亥革命后，官方纪年标准由农历改为格里历。
en: After the Xinhai Revolution, the official calendar-reckoning standard was changed from the lunar calendar to the Gregorian calendar.

text: 华夏新年与朝鲜新年、越南新年、琉球新年和明治维新前的日本新年多数为同一日，而与藏历新年、蒙古新年同日或差一天或一月。
en: The Huaxia New Year and the Korean New Year, Vietnamese New Year, Ryukyu New Year and pre-Meiji-Restoration Japanese New Year mostly fall on the same day, while with the Tibetan New Year and Mongolian New Year it is the same day or differs by one day or one month.

text: 受汉字文化圈影响，春节在老挝、泰国、新加坡、马来西亚、印尼、菲律宾等有众多华人聚居的东南亚地区也是重要的节日。
en: Influenced by the Sinosphere, the Spring Festival is also an important festival in Southeast Asian regions where large numbers of ethnic Chinese live together, such as Laos, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines.

text: 在中国大陆、香港、澳门、台湾、新加坡、马来西亚、印度尼西亚、朝鲜半岛、越南、菲律宾、毛里求斯、苏里南等地，农历新年都是法定假期。
en: In mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Korean Peninsula, Vietnam, the Philippines, Mauritius, Suriname and other places, the Lunar New Year is a statutory holiday.

text: 纽约曼哈顿华埠的中国新年游行是除亚洲以外规模最大的中国新年活动。
en: The Chinese New Year parade of Manhattan Chinatown in New York is the largest Chinese New Year event outside Asia.

text: 春节于2023年成为联合国假日，并于2024年以“春节——中国人庆祝传统新年的社会习俗”的名义列为人类非物质文化遗产代表作。
en: The Spring Festival became a United Nations holiday in 2023, and in 2024 was inscribed as a Representative of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity under the name 'Spring Festival, social practices of the Chinese people in celebration of traditional new year'.

text: 农历正月初一为一年之首，故称“岁首”，又称“年节”、“元旦”、“元正”、“元朔”、“元日”、“正旦”、“新正”、“新春”、“年节”、“履新”。
en: The first day of the first lunar month is the head of the year, therefore [it is] called 'suishou', also called 'nianjie', 'yuandan', 'yuanzheng', 'yuanshuo', 'yuanri', 'zhengdan', 'xinzheng', 'xinchun', 'nianjie', 'lüxin'.

text: 台湾话习称“新正”（sin-tsiann）、“开正”（khui-tsiann），庆祝活动叫“过年”（kuè-nî）。
en: Taiwanese customarily calls [it] 'sin-tsiann', 'khui-tsiann'; the celebrations are called 'kuè-nî'.
